walkthroughs.body_html:
Measurements & Errors — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Measurements & Errors brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Measurements & Errors.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A car travels 4 km north then 3 km east. What is its displacement magnitude?
options: 7 km
5 km
1 km
25 km

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
options: Acceleration
Momentum
Kinetic energy
Weight

mcqs.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is most ionising?
options: Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Gamma is most ionising because it can travel furthest and pass through almost anything.
Alpha radiation — large, doubly charged particles cause the most ionisation per unit distance.

mcqs.q: If a car has negative acceleration, what does that necessarily mean?
options: The number of turns in the coil alone.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.
Negative acceleration always means the car is slowing down.
Its acceleration is in the negative direction (often opposite to the chosen positive direction); it may be slowing down or speeding up in reverse.

mcqs.q: According to Faraday's law, what determines the size of the induced emf in a coil?
options: The strength of the magnetic field alone.
The number of turns in the coil alone.
The rate of change of magnetic flux linkage through the coil.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Acceleration”?
options: Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
The vector from an initial to a final position; the straight-line change in position.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Resolving vectors”?
options: A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.
Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.

options: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
A quantity with magnitude only, such as mass, time, speed, or energy.
Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Displacement”?

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Velocity”?
options: Rate of change of displacement with respect to time, measured in m s⁻¹.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
Splitting a vector into perpendicular components, typically using F cos θ and F sin θ.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Scalar”?
options: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, such as velocity, force, or displacement.
Rate of change of velocity with respect to time, measured in m s⁻².
